candidates.label: creditText
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a creative work and the text used to credit associated persons or organizations. Also called: attribution text, credit line, acknowledgment. Examples: "Movie" credit text "Directed by...", "Photograph" credit text "Photo by John Doe", "Research Paper" credit text "Funding provided by...". Distinct from creator, which identifies the primary author/creator.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: ccRecipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: leiCode
candidates.comment: A Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) code relation between an organization and its unique identifier as defined in ISO 17442. Also called: LEI, legal entity ID, ISO 17442 identifier. Examples: "Acme Corp leiCode 549300XXXXXX", "Global Bank leiCode 213800XXXXXX", "Tech Solutions Inc leiCode 894500XXXXXX".

candidates.label: bccRecipient
candidates.comment: A contact point, organization, or person who is a blind carbon copy recipient of a message. Also called: blind copy recipient, hidden recipient. Examples: "Message 'Email' bccRecipient 'Compliance Department'", "Message 'Newsletter' bccRecipient 'Marketing Team'". Distinct from recipient and ccRecipient, which are visible to other recipients.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

chosen_property.label: instrument
chosen_property.justification: Instrument property (Action → Thing) fits the use of a software application as a tool for decryption

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: archiveHeld
candidates.comment: An archive held relation between an archive organization and a collection, fonds, or item maintained by it. Also called archival holding, collection maintained, item preserved. Examples: "The National Archives' archive held is 'Presidential Papers'.", "The historical society's archive held is 'Local Family Records'."

candidates.label: conditionsOfAccess
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, detailing the natural language conditions affecting its availability or access methods. Also called "access restrictions", "availability terms", "usage conditions". Examples: "Archival document conditionsOfAccess 'Available by appointment only'", "Digital artwork conditionsOfAccess 'Requires institutional login'".

candidates.label: documentation
candidates.comment: A documentation relation between a web API and a creative work or URL providing further details about it. Also called "API documentation", "technical guide", "developer docs". Examples: "Web API 'Weather API' documentation 'example.com/weatherapi/docs'", "Payment Gateway API documentation 'CreativeWork describing endpoints'", "Mapping API documentation 'URL to usage guide'".

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: datasetTimeInterval
candidates.comment: A temporal applicability relation between a dataset and its relevant time range. Also called: dataset time range, temporal coverage, data period. Examples: "Census Data" dataset time interval "2011", "Historical Weather Data" dataset time interval "1950-2000", "Economic Survey" dataset time interval "2022-01-01/2022-12-31".

candidates.label: sdLicense
candidates.comment: The license document, often specified by a URL, that governs the use of the structured data within a creative work. Also called structured data license, metadata license, data usage terms. Examples: `Dataset Markup` sdLicense `CreativeWork: Open Data License`, `Article Structured Data` sdLicense `URL to Creative Commons license`, `Recipe JSON-LD` sdLicense `URL to specific terms`. Distinct from `license`, which is the license for the creative work itself.

chosen_property.justification: HasPart property (CreativeWork → CreativeWork) fits the inclusion of decryption tasks in a research project

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

chosen_property.justification: Mint 'containsContentAbout' for the manuscript's content about a person or clip

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: originalMediaContextDescription
candidates.comment: Background information that aids in better interpretation of a media object, especially for decontextualized content in a media review. Also called media context, original context, background description. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaContextDescription 'Video was originally posted on TikTok in 2020.'", "Image Review B originalMediaContextDescription 'Photo taken during a protest in 2018, not current event.'", "Audio Review C originalMediaContextDescription 'Clip is from a satirical podcast, not a news broadcast.'". Distinct from reviewBody, which is the main text of the review.

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: articleBody
candidates.comment: The main textual content of an article. Also called: article content, body text, main text. Examples: "Article 'News Report' articleBody 'The city council voted...'", "Article 'Research Paper' articleBody 'Our findings indicate...'", "Article 'Blog Post' articleBody 'Today I learned...'."

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: text
candidates.comment: The primary textual content of a creative work. Also called "content text", "body text", "written content", "main text". Examples: "The article has text 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...'", "The book's text is its full narrative", "This creative work's text is its script."

candidates.label: containsSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a radio, TV, or video game series and a creative work season that is part of it. Also called "includes season", "has season", "season of series". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: caption
candidates.comment: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".

candidates.label: employerOverview
candidates.comment: An employer overview relation between a job posting and the text describing the employer, career opportunities, and work environment. Also called "company description", "about the employer", "workplace culture". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employerOverview 'Innovative tech company with great benefits'", "Job 'Marketing Manager' employerOverview 'Fast-paced startup environment'", "Job 'Nurse' employerOverview 'Leading hospital with focus on patient care'".

candidates.label: text
candidates.comment: The primary textual content of a creative work. Also called "content text", "body text", "written content", "main text". Examples: "The article has text 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...'", "The book's text is its full narrative", "This creative work's text is its script."

candidates.label: accessibilitySummary
candidates.comment: An accessibility summary relation between a creative work and a human-readable text describing its accessibility features and deficiencies. Also called accessibility overview, access statement, accessibility report. Examples: "A website's accessibility summary states 'Short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users'.", "A document's accessibility summary notes 'Fully navigable by keyboard'."

candidates.label: abstract
candidates.comment: An abstract relation between a creative work and a short text summarizing its content. Also called summary, synopsis, précis, overview. Examples: "A research paper's abstract describes its findings.", "A movie's abstract outlines its plot."

candidates.label: reviewBody
candidates.comment: The main textual content or narrative of a review. Also called review text, review content, review description. Examples: `Customer Review` reviewBody `"This product exceeded my expectations..."`, `Book Review` reviewBody `"A compelling narrative with rich characters..."`, `Restaurant Review` reviewBody `"The ambiance was lovely, but the food was bland."`.

candidates.label: unitText
candidates.comment: A unit text relation between a property value, quantitative value, type and quantity node, or unit price specification and a string indicating its unit of measurement. Also called unit description, measurement label, custom unit. Examples: "QuantitativeValue unitText 'kilograms'", "PropertyValue unitText 'persons'", "UnitPriceSpecification unitText 'dollars'". Distinct from unitCode, which uses a standard code for the unit of measurement.

candidates.label: bookEdition
candidates.comment: A textual description of the edition of a book. Also called: edition number, publication edition. Examples: "Book 'The Lord of the Rings' bookEdition 'First Edition'", "Book 'Textbook' bookEdition '2nd Edition'."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: expectedPrognosis
candidates.comment: An expected prognosis relation between a medical condition and its likely short-term or long-term outcome. Also called: anticipated outcome, predicted course, outlook. Examples: "Common Cold" expected prognosis "Full recovery within a week", "Type 2 Diabetes" expected prognosis "Manageable with lifestyle changes and medication", "Stage 4 Cancer" expected prognosis "Poor, with limited treatment options".

candidates.label: yield
candidates.comment: A yield relation between a how-to guide and a quantitative value or text, specifying the quantity or type of output produced by following the instructions. Also called output quantity, resulting amount, production yield. Examples: HowToRecipe yield "12 cookies", HowToCraft yield "1 paper airplane", HowToGuide yield "5 liters of jam".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim

A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: studySubject

Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy

Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: study

Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: studyDesign

candidates.label: measurementMethod
candidates.comment: A measurement method relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the specific method used for measurement. Also called: method of measurement, specific technique, measurement approach. Examples: "Temperature Dataset measurementMethod 'Thermocouple'", "Survey Data measurementMethod 'Likert Scale'", "Chemical Analysis measurementMethod 'Spectrophotometry'". candidates.label: deliveryMethod

Examples: "Online Purchase" delivery method "Standard Shipping", "Document Send" delivery method "Email", "Package Tracking" delivery method "Courier Service".

candidates.label: trialDesign

Examples: "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'RandomizedControlledTrial'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'ObservationalStudy'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'DoubleBlindTrial'".

candidates.label: imagingTechnique
candidates.comment: An imaging technique relation between an imaging test and the medical imaging technique employed. Also called scanning technique, imaging method, diagnostic imaging. Examples: "An imaging test uses an imaging technique of MRI.", "The scan employs an imaging technique of X-ray.", "This test specifies its imaging technique."

candidates.label: algorithm
